title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is part of Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', his own approach to what later became the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. He studies an automorphism \hat\varphi, coming from Gal(\bar Q/Q) or a GT-type element, of an extended profinite Teichmüller group \hat{\mathfrak S}^{+}_{0,3}. This group is an extension of \mathfrak S_3 by \pi_{0,\hat3}, the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,\infty}. Inside it: \rho is the order-3 rotation, \sigma_\infty and \tau_\infty are elements attached to the point at infinity, and \rho also acts by conjugation.

Parameters. The 'coarse parameter' \xi (a value of \hat\varphi on a canonical element) satisfies the 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi)=1. This is exactly the 1-cocycle (norm) condition for the Z/3 action. The 'delicate parameters' are \alpha and \beta, with \tilde\alpha=\alpha\tau_\infty^{\alpha_3}. They are expected to satisfy \xi=\alpha\rho(\alpha)^{-1} and \eta=\beta\sigma_\infty(\beta)^{-1}, i.e. the cocycles are coboundaries. Integer invariants i, \alpha_3 \in Z/12 and j' \in Z/3 record the images in \mathfrak S_3 (formulas (51) on the previous page).

The page. Previous formulas give:
- (49)/(10): \hat\varphi(\xi)=\beta\sigma_\infty^{i}.
- (47): \hat\varphi(\rho^{-1}(\xi))=\rho^{j'}\sigma_\infty^{\alpha_3}\tilde\alpha^{-1}.

The cocycle relation, conjugated cyclically, gives \rho^{-1}(\xi)\xi=\rho(\xi)^{-1}. Multiplying the two formulas therefore gives \hat\varphi(\rho(\xi)^{-1})=\rho^{j'}\sigma_\infty^{\alpha_3}\tilde\alpha^{-1}\beta\sigma_\infty^{i}. Inverting gives (52): \hat\varphi(\rho(\xi)) expressed through \beta^{-1}\tilde\alpha, and solving gives (53): \beta^{-1}\tilde\alpha=(\beta^{-1}\alpha)\tau_\infty^{\alpha_3} in terms of \hat\varphi(\rho(\xi)).

Conclusion drawn. The three principal delicate parameters \beta, \alpha and \beta^{-1}\alpha are read off directly from the values of \hat\varphi at \xi, \rho^{-1}(\xi) and \rho^{-2}(\xi)=\rho(\xi). Grothendieck remarks that this would probably let one avoid the still-unproved 'delicate' results \xi=\alpha\rho(\alpha)^{-1} and \eta=\beta\sigma_\infty(\beta)^{-1} when justifying the introduction of \alpha and \beta. In those results the parameters are defined by trivializing the cocycles, i.e. a nonabelian H^1 / conjugacy-of-torsion statement. The next page recapitulates as (54) and specializes to \alpha_3=0.

Purpose. Express Drinfeld-style 'f'-type parameters (delicate) in terms of the coarse invariant \xi, i.e. a parametrization of the action on the genus-0, 3-point Teichmüller group by explicit formulas.
errors: Inverting \rho^{j'}\sigma_\infty^{\alpha_3}\tilde\alpha^{-1}\beta\sigma_\infty^{i} should give \sigma_\infty^{-i}(\beta^{-1}\tilde\alpha)\sigma_\infty^{-\alpha_3}\rho^{-j'}. In (52) the signs of the exponents of \sigma_\infty appear to be dropped, which is harmless only if the relevant powers coincide.

In (53), solving (52) for \beta^{-1}\tilde\alpha should give \sigma_\infty^{i}\hat\varphi(\rho(\xi))\rho^{j'}\sigma_\infty^{\alpha_3}. Grothendieck writes \sigma_\infty^{i}\hat\varphi(\rho(\xi))\sigma_\infty^{\alpha_3}\rho^{\pm j'}, with the order of \rho^{j'} and \sigma_\infty^{\alpha_3} swapped (they do not commute in general) and sign ambiguities. These are sloppy bookkeeping, not conceptual errors.
There is a hesitation over which formulas are multiplied ('(47) et (50)' crossed toward '(47) et (40)/(10)'). Mathematically it must be (47) together with (10)/(49), the formula for \hat\varphi(\xi).

ideas.what: 3-cycle relation \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi)=1 for the coarse parameter, rewritten as \rho^{-1}(\xi)\xi=\rho(\xi)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: hexagon relation of GT (Drinfeld's relation II); 1-cocycle/norm condition for Z/3 acting on \hat F_2
ideas.where_published: GT program alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), no explicit formulas there

ideas.what: Explicit expression of the 'delicate' parameters \alpha, \beta, \beta^{-1}\alpha via values of \hat\varphi on \xi, \rho^{-1}(\xi), \rho(\xi), together with Z/12 and Z/3 discrete invariants
ideas.modern_name: parametrization of elements of \hat{GT} acting on \hat{SL}_2(Z)-type groups (compare Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps version of GT)

ideas.what: The 'delicate unproved results' \xi=\alpha\rho(\alpha)^{-1}, \eta=\beta\sigma_\infty(\beta)^{-1}, i.e. cocycles for finite cyclic actions on profinite free groups being coboundaries
ideas.modern_name: nonabelian H^1 vanishing; conjugacy of torsion elements/finite subgroups in profinite virtually free groups such as \hat{PSL_2(Z)}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Herfort–Ribes, Zalesskii (torsion in profinite free products, 1980s); used in Lochak–Schneps / LNS

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags as 'délicats non encore démontrés' the statements that the cocycles \xi (for Z/3) and \eta (for Z/2) are coboundaries. These are equivalent to conjugacy of order-3 and order-2 lifts in the profinite semidirect product, which follows from the later Herfort–Ribes/Zalesskii theorems on torsion in profinite free products. His alternative strategy is to bypass these results by expressing \alpha, \beta directly through values of \hat\varphi.
missed.quote: de faire appel à des résultats délicats non encore démontrés, du type ζ=αρ(α)^{-1}, η=βσ_∞(β)^{-1}, pour justifier l'introduction de ces paramètres α, β
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's independent pre-Drinfeld identification of the key group-theoretic input of GT theory and an explicit coboundary-free parametrization. This is mainly of historical interest, since the input is now known.

missed.claim: He wants the discrete invariants (i, \alpha_3, j') \in Z/12\times Z/12\times Z/3 and the delicate parameters expressed through multipliers/cyclotomic data. The thread is left open on these pages.
missed.quote: On peut considérer que les trois "paramètres délicats" principaux sont les quantités β, α et β^{-1}α
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. Analogous normalizations exist in the GT literature (the \lambda parameter and the role of 12 via SL_2(Z) abelianization), so little is likely new.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine algebraic manipulation within Grothendieck's own (unpublished) proto-GT computations. Historically interesting as a precursor of Drinfeld/LNS and for explicitly isolating the torsion-conjugacy input, but it contains no result clearly absent from the later literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: the relation reads \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi)=1; the crossed-out text is '\rho^{-1}(\xi)=\xi\rho(\xi)'.
'\rho J'' should be read as \rho^{j'} (exponent j' \in Z/3), consistent with formula (51) on the previous page.
The line 'en multipliant (47) et (50)[?]' is not a separate line; the page has a single phrase 'on trouve donc, en multipliant (47) et (10)' (the second number is probably (10) or (49), not (40)).
